title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
summary: Every analysis was driven over a real Android project of 5000 files instead of test fixtures. Expand Selection, test source sets and the Logcat process filter all had bugs only real code showed.

highlights.title: Expand Selection lands on the cursor
highlights.description: On a data class whose parameters each carry an annotation on the line above, putting the cursor on the annotation selected the previous property. Twenty four files of the project were affected.

highlights.title: Unit tests in a build variant
highlights.description: The project keeps them in `src/testReplica/java`, and 155 real test files were read as production code. The rule is now anchored where Gradle puts the source set name, the directory right after `src`.

highlights.title: A reopened file shows itself
highlights.description: Closing a file without saving and reopening it showed the structure of the previous session, and when the earlier buffer was longer the Outline threw and emptied itself.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: A production file named like a test source set, `androidTestHelper.kt`, is no longer hidden from Go to Definition.
The Logcat process filter keeps the main process instead of retiring it first when the app spawns many processes.
Reconnecting to the device already selected no longer replays the whole device buffer.
A state write at the very end of a file is counted, and the lens offers the place to jump to.

sections.heading: Notes
bullets: The sweep now runs over 3187 Kotlin files, 1901 Java files, 51 manifests and 410 vector drawables, and reports zero anomaly.
